subtitle: When Harishena’s Thunder Faded into Silence

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a fading battlefield merging into a ruined palace
panels.action: Harishena stands in armour at the centre of a dusty field, his sword lowered, as behind him victorious standards blur and dissolve into the crumbling walls of a deserted Vakataka palace under a red dusk sky.

dialogue.text: Harishena of the Vakatakas is praised for subduing seven regions—yet within a generation, his empire is gone and the record falls silent.

i18n.hi: वत्सगुल्म के वाकाटक हरिषेण को सात प्रदेश दबाने वाला कहा गया, पर एक पीढ़ी में ही साम्राज्य गायब, लेख भी चुप हो जाते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in from map-like landscape to young king in council
panels.action: A stylised map of the western Deccan and central India, with tiny carved hills and rivers, lies spread on a low table; young Harishena, crowned and alert, leans over it in a lamplit hall at Vatsagulma.

dialogue.text: Late fifth-century India is a chessboard of powers—Guptas to the north, regional kings to the west and east, and in the plateau of the Deccan, the Vakatakas of Vatsagulma under Harishena.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी के अंत में भारत मानो शतरंज की बिसात था—उत्तरे में गुप्त, पूरब–पश्चिम में प्रादेशिक राजा, और दक्खिन की पट्टी पर हरिषेण का वत्सगुल्म वाकाटक राज।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Harishena’s face, half-lit, with war map in foreground
panels.action: Harishena’s face fills the frame, one side in warm lamplight, the other in shadow; in the foreground, wooden markers shaped like forts and elephants stand on the map at Kuntala and Avanti.

dialogue.text: We know little of his youth, but his minister Varahadeva later inscribes that Harishena subdued Kuntala, Avanti, Kalinga, Kosala, Lata, Andhra and Trikuta.

i18n.hi: उसके बचपन का बहुत कम पता है, पर मंत्री वराहदेव बाद में लिखवाता है कि हरिषेण ने कुत्तल, अवन्ति, कलिंग, कोसाल, लाट, आंध्र और त्रिकूट को झुका लिया।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of Deccan plateau with marching columns
panels.action: From high above, long columns of troops and elephants snake across the rocky Deccan plateau towards a distant fortified town, banners fluttering, dust hanging in the air as the sun burns overhead.

dialogue.text: These names are not gentle hints of influence. In Varahadeva’s Cave 16 inscription, they are victories—regions he claims were brought under Harishena’s power.

i18n.hi: ये नाम बस हल्का असर नहीं, वराहदेव की गुफा १६ की शिलालेख में ये साफ़ फ़तहें हैं—इलाके जो वह हरिषेण की ताकत के नीचे लाए गए बताता है।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of siege scene from outside city walls
panels.action: At the foot of a thick stone wall, Vakataka soldiers raise ladders and shields while stone missiles arc from above; Harishena rides along the lines on a caparisoned elephant, arm raised to direct the assault.

dialogue.text: Kuntala, in the western Deccan; Avanti, around Malwa; Kalinga and Kosala, straddling the eastern coast and central forests—each meant walls, citadels and kings who had to yield or be crushed.

i18n.hi: कुत्तल, पश्चिमी दक्खिन; अवन्ति, मालवा के आस–पास; कलिंग और कोसाल, पूरबी तट और बीच के जंगल—हर जगह किले, दुर्ग और राजा जो झुकते, वरना कुचले जाते।

panels.shot: wide shot of coastal plain with army approaching a distant city
panels.action: On a humid coastal plain dotted with palms and rivers, a Vakataka army advances toward a walled port town, its harbour filled with masts; the sky is heavy with monsoon clouds.

dialogue.text: Lata and Andhra, rich coastal tracts of trade and salt breezes, lay along key routes; to hold them was to grip the western and eastern sea-belt.

i18n.hi: लाट और आंध्र, नमकीन हवाओं और व्यापार से भरे समुद्री पट्टे, अहम राहों पर थे; इन्हें पकड़ना मतलब पश्चिम और पूरब की सागरी कमान थामना।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of fortress atop hills symbolising Trikuta
panels.action: A rugged, triple-peaked hill range rises under a clear sky, crowned by a compact stone fortress; below, Harishena looks up from horseback, a stern resolve in his eyes.

dialogue.text: Trikuta, likely in the western coast hills where the Traikutakas issued coins, is also listed. Their coinage breaks in the late fifth century—some scholars see Harishena’s pressure in that silence.

i18n.hi: त्रिकूट, शायद पश्चिमी तटीय पहाड़ियों में, जहाँ त्रैकूटक सिक्के चलाते थे, भी गिना है; उनके सिक्के पाँचवीं सदी के अंत तक टूट जाते हैं—कुछ विद्वान इसे हरिषेण की मार का मौन निशान मानते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate interior of palace with Harishena and Varahadeva near a pillar
panels.action: Inside a richly painted hall, Harishena stands beside a tall stone pillar; Varahadeva, in simple yet dignified attire, gestures respectfully toward a parchment sketch showing a list of conquered regions.

dialogue.text: We hear these boasts not from Harishena’s own mouth, but through Varahadeva, his minister, in an inscription at Ajanta—part eulogy, part record of campaigns.

i18n.hi: ये शेख़ियाँ हमें हरिषेण की ज़ुबान से नहीं, मंत्री वराहदेव की, अजन्ता की एक शिला से मिलती हैं—आधा गुणगान, आधा युद्ध-वृत्तांत।

panels.shot: sweeping interior wide of Ajanta cave under construction
panels.action: Craftsmen chip away at a massive rock-cut hall, scaffolds clinging to the walls; Harishena stands at the entrance of the future Cave 16, watching as dust and stone flakes rain down in shafts of light.

dialogue.text: While armies marched, patronage flowed. Under Harishena, Ajanta’s great caves—like Cave 16, dedicated by Varahadeva—were carved into the cliff, mixing devotion with royal prestige.

i18n.hi: जब सेनाएँ बढ़ीं, दान भी बहा; हरिषेण के समय अजन्ता की बड़ी गुफाएँ—जैसे वराहदेव की समर्पित गुफा १६—चट्टान में काटी गईं, भक्ति और शाही शान साथ–साथ उभरी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Harishena seated on throne, envoys kneeling
panels.action: In a grand throne room adorned with murals, Harishena sits upright on a lion-footed seat; two envoys from different regions bow before him, each holding a casket of tribute and an arm-ring of allegiance.

dialogue.text: Victory meant more than battle smoke. It meant tribute, alliances, governors in distant towns—and kings or chiefs compelled to accept Vakataka overlordship, however uneasy.

i18n.hi: फ़तह का मतलब सिर्फ़ धुएँ वाली जंग नहीं; इसका मतलब कर, संधियाँ, दूर शहरों में सूबेदार—और राजा–नरेश जो मन मसोसकर भी वाकाटक आधिपत्य मानने पर मजबूर हुए।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Harishena’s hand over a map showing vast domain
panels.action: Harishena’s hand rests heavily on a map now shaded wide, from the western coast through Malwa to the eastern tracts, small carved crowns marking subordinate rulers.

dialogue.text: By the later days of his reign, the Vatsagulma branch of the Vakatakas stood at what seems their widest reach, their name carried from the western sea to central forests and beyond.

i18n.hi: उसके राज के उत्तरार्ध में वत्सगुल्म वाकाटक शायद अपनी चरम हद तक फैल चुके थे, उनका नाम पश्चिमी सागर से लेकर बीच के जंगलों और आगे तक गूँज रहा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Harishena older, alone at night in balcony
panels.action: An older Harishena, features lined, stands at a palace balcony at night, looking out over a torch-lit city; behind him, a single unattended child’s seat sits empty in the shadows.

dialogue.text: Yet here the record darkens. We do not know his sons’ names, nor see clear succession grants; the inscription praises him, but is silent about who will sit next on his throne.

i18n.hi: पर यहीं से पन्ना धुंधला हो जाता है; न उसके बेटों के नाम मिलते हैं, न साफ़ उत्तराधिकार के दान-पत्र; शिला बस हरिषेण की तारीफ़ करती है, सिंहासन के अगले वारिस पर चुप है।

panels.shot: symbolic shot of abandoned royal seal on dust-covered throne
panels.action: A once-polished throne stands in a dim hall, its cushions dulled with dust; on the seat lies a Vakataka signet ring, toppled and half-buried in a thin layer of grit.

dialogue.text: Harishena dies—around the early sixth century, scholars infer—and suddenly, inscriptions bearing his line vanish. The Vakataka voice falls quiet, as if cut mid-sentence.

i18n.hi: हरिषेण मरता है—विद्वान इसे छठी सदी की शुरुआत मानते हैं—और अचानक उसकी वंश-रेखा वाले अभिलेख ग़ायब हो जाते हैं; वाकाटक की आवाज़ मानो आधे वाक्य में कटकर खामोश हो जाती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of fractured map showing Vakataka lands splintering
panels.action: The earlier map of the Vakataka domain appears again, but now cracks radiate through it like shattered pottery, the colours of different regions pulling apart from a fading central core.

dialogue.text: There is no chronicler to tell us why. Scholars point to overextension, rival claimants, or pressure near Malwa from the Hunas—but the stones and copperplates do not name a final war.

i18n.hi: कोई समकालीन इतिहासकार नहीं बताता क्यों; विद्वान ज़्यादा फैलाव, भीतर के दावेदार, या मालवा के पास हूणों का दबाव कहते हैं—पर पत्थर और ताम्रपत्र किसी आख़िरी जंग का नाम नहीं लेते।

panels.shot: suggestive montage: distant northern battle, court intrigue, and rising new king
panels.action: Three faint scenes overlap: a northern army clashing in a distant plain, shadowy courtiers whispering in a lamplit hall, and a new Deccan king raising a banner over a hill-fort to the southwest.

dialogue.text: Upinder Singh, V. V. Mirashi and others suggest a mix of threats—Huna turmoil near Malwa, internal weakness, and the rise of new powers like the early Chalukyas—but all as careful inference, not recorded verdict.

i18n.hi: उपिंदर सिंह, वी. वी. मिराशी और दूसरे विद्वान मिलीजुली मार मानते हैं—मालवा के पास हूण हलचल, अंदरूनी कमजोरी, और आरम्भिक चालुक्यों जैसे नए ताक़तवर—पर सब अनुमान, दर्ज फ़ैसला नहीं।

panels.shot: wide landscape shot of western Deccan with Chalukya standard in foreground
panels.action: Over the rocky plains and rivers of the western Deccan, a fresh standard bearing an early Chalukya emblem rises into view, while far behind, an older Vakataka banner droops and slips out of frame.

dialogue.text: What the record does show is this: soon after Harishena’s time, early Chalukya power spreads across the western Deccan, filling the political space where Vakataka control once stood.

i18n.hi: जो साफ़ दिखता है, वह यह कि हरिषेण के बाद ही जल्द, शुरुआती चालुक्य शक्ति पश्चिमी दक्खिन में फैलती है, वहीं जगह भरती जहाँ कभी वाकाटक का नियंत्रण खड़ा था।

panels.shot: somber interior of Ajanta cave, empty and half-finished
panels.action: Inside an Ajanta hall, unfinished sculptures and blank wall spaces lie in silence; tools rest abandoned on the floor, a thin film of dust softening their edges as sunlight streams in from the veranda.

dialogue.text: At Ajanta too, the rhythm halts. Walter Spink notes how work on the great caves, so intense under Harishena, stops abruptly—another trace of patronage cut off and an empire’s end without a recorded scene.

i18n.hi: अजन्ता में भी ताल टूटता है; वॉल्टर स्पिंक दिखाते हैं कैसे हरिषेण के ज़ोरदार संरक्षण में चल रहा गुफाओं का काम अचानक थम जाता है—जैसे दान सूख गया हो, और साम्राज्य अंत हुआ हो, बिना मंचित आख़िरी दृश्य के।

panels.shot: ghostly superimposition of Harishena’s figure in the empty cave
panels.action: Harishena’s translucent figure is faintly superimposed over the empty Ajanta hall, standing where Varahadeva’s inscription would be, face unreadable as carved Buddhas look on from the shadows.

dialogue.text: Varahadeva’s Cave 16 inscription still proclaims his master’s conquests, carved in stone; yet outside, the dynasty’s political body has already faded, leaving the words to outlast the king.

i18n.hi: वराहदेव की गुफा १६ की शिला अब भी स्वामी की फतहें पत्थर पर गाती है; पर गुफा के बाहर, वंश की राजनीतिक देह कब की मुरझा चुकी, राजा के बाद बस शब्द ही बचे हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide of modern sky over Ajanta cliffs with Harishena’s silhouette fading
panels.action: The camera looks up at the Ajanta cliff face under a clear sky; high above, the faint silhouette of Harishena’s profile dissolves into the rock as birds wheel past the cave mouths.

dialogue.text: Harishena’s wars pushed the Vakataka name across half a subcontinent, yet without a secure succession and recorded ending, his empire slipped away—reminding us how swift conquest can be, and how fragile its memory.

i18n.hi: हरिषेण की जंगों ने वाकाटक नाम को आधे उपमहाद्वीप तक पहुँचा दिया, पर ठोस उत्तराधिकार और दर्ज अंत के बिना, उसका साम्राज्य हाथ से फिसल गया—याद दिलाता है कि जीत जितनी तेज़ हो सकती है, उसकी याद उतनी ही नाज़ुक।

title_i18n.en: Empire at Dusk: Harishena's Wars and Fall
title_i18n.hi: सांझ का साम्राज्य: हरिषेण की जंगें और पतन

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब हरिषेण की गड़गड़ाहट थमकर सन्नाटा बन गई
